message.content:
Sure! To bake a classic chocolate cake at home, you'll typically use one of the following machines:

| Machine | Why it’s great for cakes |
|---------|--------------------------|
| **Conventional Oven** | Most people have this already. It provides even heat from all sides—perfect for a traditional rise and golden crust. |
| **Convection Oven** | Adds a fan that circulates hot air, cooking more evenly and often slightly faster than a conventional oven. Great if your regular oven tends to brown unevenly. |
| **Microwave + Steam Function** | If you're short on time, many modern microwaves now come with a “steam” setting that helps keep baked goods moist. You’ll still get good results but the texture will differ slightly from a fully baked oven cake. |
| **Air Fryer / Mini Convection Oven** | Small countertop units work well for single-layer cakes or cupcakes. Just watch the timer closely—they cook quickly! |

### Quick Tips:
* Preheat the oven before putting the batter inside – most recipes recommend around 350 °F (175 °C).
* Use parchment paper or grease & flour the pan so the cake releases easily after baking.
* Check doneness with a toothpick inserted into the center—it should come out clean when ready.

If you’re looking for a quick, no‑fuss option, a standard electric oven works best for achieving that fluffy crumb and rich chocolate flavor typical of a homemade chocolate cake. Happy baking!
